commit.message:
feat(pstack): add the statechart skill to draw TLA+ models as charts (#741)

* Add the statechart skill to pstack

Draws what a user sees as a Mermaid statechart generated from a TLA+
model. TLC checks the reader's rules as invariants. Each state is marked
works, still wrong, or fixed by an open change, and each counterexample
class is drawn as a numbered path. The skill also turns an agreed chart
into a TLA+ skeleton and compares the drawn chart with the agreed one.

Bumps pstack to 0.15.30 and regenerates the Claude Code harness tree.

* Fix the review findings in the statechart skill

- Check each rule in its own TLC run. The generated cfg names no rule,
  and a comment in it lists the rules.
- Refuse TLC output from a run that failed or stopped early, and read
  counterexamples that a start state breaks.
- Count steps that change nothing when a state is settled, number bugs
  that only the fixed model has after the current bugs, and escape
  quotes in captions.
- Compare parallel regions as one machine, and refuse charts that were
  not drawn for comparison.
- Refuse final states and duplicate captions, read class shorthand and
  states first named inside a composite, and match a never line to an
  exact state.
- Rewrite SKILL.md to match, and run the skill script tests in CI.

* Refuse a -- outside a composite in statechart charts

A -- at the top level of a chart opened a second root part that the
parser never read, so every region after it was dropped. chart-to-tla
wrote a one-region skeleton, and compare-charts could print "same".
parseMermaid now refuses the chart. A unit test covers parseMermaid,
chart-to-tla, and compare-charts.

Co-authored-by: lauren <poteto@users.noreply.github.com>

* Exit 2 when compare-charts cannot read a chart

compare-charts let a read or parse error escape, so a chart it could
not read exited 1, the code for charts that differ. It now prints the
file and the reason to stderr and exits 2, as SKILL.md says for a
refused chart. Exit 1 now means only that the charts differ.

Co-authored-by: lauren <poteto@users.noreply.github.com>

* Update the statechart skill to its current version

Replace the skill, its scripts, and its tests with the current version.
statechart.mjs runs the whole flow with from-spec and from-chart, and its
--help replaces the old Setup section. New features are a code-against-spec
audit (--against), nested state boxes, parallel regions, guards, scoped
charts, timer labels, and legend groups and colors chosen in the mapping.

TLC comes from TLA2TOOLS and JAVA only. Without TLA2TOOLS, the scripts point
to the TLA+ releases page and exit 2.

Co-authored-by: lauren <poteto@users.noreply.github.com>

* Exit 2 when --png cannot render a chart

A failed mermaid-cli render printed "could not render" but still exited 0,
or 0 with --expect-broken, so callers reported PNGs that did not exist.
finish() now exits 2 whenever --png renders fewer PNGs than charts, and
keeps the files it wrote. The --help exit codes say so, and a new test
covers it with an npx that cannot launch a browser.

Co-authored-by: lauren <poteto@users.noreply.github.com>

* Update the statechart skill to its latest version

Rendered charts keep their full width. An edge label writes the opening
words that its choices share once, instead of cutting the label with "…".
--full-labels replaces --all-labels, and compare-charts refuses a chart
drawn without it.

The fix replay matches each bug step by the screens and step words that
the reader sees, and two states get at most one arrow. Each rule also runs
as a TLC CONSTRAINT, so a rule that stays broken stops at its first bad
state instead of flooding TLC with counterexamples.

statechart.mjs passes its arguments and models through functions instead
of module globals. The --png exit code from the previous commit is now
part of the source.

Co-authored-by: lauren <poteto@users.noreply.github.com>

* Update the statechart skill: safe output folder, its TLA+ model, and the comment and assignment cleanups

Co-authored-by: lauren <poteto@users.noreply.github.com>

* Drop a comment in the public findTlc that only describes the code

Co-authored-by: lauren <poteto@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>
